option_description: Attestation that the data tier (DB instances, cache nodes, object stores) is NOT directly reachable from any untrusted/public network. Insecure when true.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Direct public exposure of the data store" (T1190) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when data_store_publicly_routable is true. Public reachability of a data-tier port lets an attacker target a service CVE without ever traversing the application-tier PEP.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a public/untrusted vantage point (not inside the VPC), port-scan the data-tier endpoints — relational DB port (5432/3306/1433), cache port (6379/11211), object-store port (9000), MongoDB (27017). Confirm every port filtered/closed.
how_to_obtain.command: nmap -Pn -p 5432,3306,6379,27017,9000 <data-tier-host-or-VIP>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All data-tier ports show filtered/closed from public probe; no banner, no TCP handshake completion.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-41r1 Guidelines on Firewalls

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the cloud route tables and subnet associations for the data-tier subnet. Confirm no IGW / 0.0.0.0/0 default route and no public-IP assignment on any data-tier ENI/instance.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=<data-subnet>; aws rds describe-db-instances --query 'DBInstances[*].[DBInstanceIdentifier,PubliclyAccessible]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Route table contains only intra-VPC / NAT-egress entries (no IGW target); every RDS PubliclyAccessible flag is false.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-41r1 Guidelines on Firewalls

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review every security-group / NSG / firewall rule whose destination is a data-tier resource. Confirm no rule allows source 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on a data port.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids <data-sg> --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every ingress rule scopes source to an app-tier security-group ID or a private CIDR; no public CIDR appears.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 12 Network Infrastructure Management

option_description: Attestation that every ingress path into the data tier transits the application-tier Policy Enforcement Point (API gateway, service-mesh sidecar, identity-aware proxy) — no alternate non-PEP path exists.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Direct public exposure of the data store" (T1190) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when data_tier_crossing_only_via_app_pep is false. An alternate path that skips the PEP voids per-request authn/authz on the crossing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Reachability analysis: enumerate every principal (security-group, IAM role, peering, transit gateway, VPN, Direct Connect) that can reach the data-tier endpoints. Confirm each documented path lands at an app-tier PEP and that direct paths exist only for explicitly-approved break-glass.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Single approved ingress: data-tier security group accepts only from the app-tier service identity / mesh sidecar; break-glass channel is documented, PAM-gated, disabled-by-default.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture

how_to_obtain.instruction: From an attacker-modelled foothold inside a non-app-tier workload (e.g., a CI runner, an unrelated service pod), attempt a TCP connect to the data-tier port. Repeat across each non-app-tier subnet/security-group.
how_to_obtain.command: nc -zv <data-tier-host> 5432 ; nc -zv <data-tier-host> 6379
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All connections refused / filtered. Only sources inside the app-tier security group can complete a TCP handshake on a data port.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-125B Secure Virtual Network Configuration for VM Protection

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the service-mesh / API-gateway configuration (Istio AuthorizationPolicy, Envoy filter chain, AWS API Gateway resource policy) and confirm the only routes that reach a data-tier upstream are gated by an application-tier identity claim.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get authorizationpolicy -A -o yaml | grep -A5 data-tier
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Mesh policy explicitly requires the app-tier service-account principal on every route to a data-tier upstream; no allow-all or empty principal block.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-207A ZTA Model for Cloud-Native Apps

option_description: Attestation that each app workload authenticates to the data store with its own least-privilege service identity (IAM database auth, SPIFFE SVID, per-app DB role) — not a shared superuser credential.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Anonymous/shared-credential crossing of the boundary" (T1078) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when per_workload_db_identity_used is false. A single shared DB credential gives every leaked .env / image scan the blast radius of the entire data tier.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inventory the credentials each app workload uses to reach the data tier (IaC, Helm values, Kubernetes secrets, secret-manager mappings). Confirm each app maps to its own DB role / IAM identity / SVID — not a shared 'postgres' / 'sa' / 'root'.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get secret -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}/{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -i db
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One role per app (app_orders, app_billing, ...) with distinct credentials and rotation/lease policy; no shared admin/root reused across services.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-207A ZTA Model for Cloud-Native Apps

how_to_obtain.instruction: Sample the data-tier auth log over a 24-hour window and group connections by authenticated principal. Confirm distinct principals per app rather than a single high-volume shared account.
how_to_obtain.command: psql -c "SELECT usename, count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity GROUP BY usename;" ; aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=connect
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Auth log shows N distinct app-role principals (one per app), absence of a single high-volume shared admin/root principal handling normal traffic.
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10 — Log and Monitor All Access

option_description: Attestation that credentials crossing the data-tier boundary are short-lived / dynamically issued (Vault leases, IAM session tokens, X.509 SVIDs) — not long-lived static passwords pinned in config files.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Anonymous/shared-credential crossing of the boundary" (T1078) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when data_tier_credentials_short_lived is false. Long-lived pinned credentials survive image leaks, IaC commits, and engineer offboarding indefinitely.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the secret-issuance configuration (Vault DB secrets engine, AWS Secrets Manager rotation, IAM RDS auth, SPIRE workload registration) and read each app's credential TTL / lease duration.
how_to_obtain.command: vault read database/roles/app_orders ; aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id <name> --query 'RotationRules'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each app role has a documented short TTL (typically <=24h for Vault leases, <=15min for IAM RDS auth tokens); rotation enabled with a defined interval.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Pick three application services at random and ask the operator to demonstrate where the DB password lives at runtime. Confirm it is fetched at startup (or per-connection) from a broker — not baked into a config file or environment variable that has lived for months.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Operator demonstrates a Vault/SecretsManager/IRSA fetch with a documented TTL; no long-lived static password exists in the deployment manifest.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Secrets Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: If using AWS IAM database authentication, confirm the engine has IAM auth enabled and that app workloads call GenerateDBAuthToken rather than supplying a pinned password.
how_to_obtain.command: aws rds describe-db-instances --query 'DBInstances[*].[DBInstanceIdentifier,IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled is true for every in-scope instance; app code paths use GenerateDBAuthToken / RDS IAM SDK calls.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — Protecting Data at Rest

option_description: Attestation that the app-tier role's grants on the data store are scoped to per-query need — no ALL PRIVILEGES, no s3:*, no Redis ACL +@all ~*, no superuser/db_owner/consoleAdmin.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Broken authorization at the crossing - over-privileged grants enabling bulk harvesting" (T1213) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when least_privilege_db_account is false. Wildcard grants turn a successful SQLi or credential leak into a tenancy-wide scrape.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the per-app role's grants on each data engine and confirm they list specific schemas/tables/buckets/key-patterns with the minimum verbs — never SUPERUSER, ALL PRIVILEGES, consoleAdmin, or +@all ~*.
how_to_obtain.command: psql -c "\du" -c "SELECT * FROM information_schema.role_table_grants WHERE grantee='app_orders';" ; mysql -e "SHOW GRANTS FOR 'app'@'%';" ; mc admin policy info ALIAS app-policy ; redis-cli ACL GETUSER app
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Grants enumerate explicit schemas/tables/buckets/key-patterns and verbs (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on named objects); absence of SUPERUSER/ALL PRIVILEGES/consoleAdmin/+@all ~*.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1078 Valid Accounts

how_to_obtain.instruction: For S3/MinIO buckets backing the data tier, evaluate the bucket policy and IAM role policy together — confirm no Action: "s3:*" combined with Resource: "arn:aws:s3:::*".
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam get-role-policy --role-name <app-role> --policy-name <inline> ; aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <data-bucket>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy enumerates explicit object actions (s3:GetObject, s3:PutObject) on named bucket-and-prefix resources; no wildcard action or resource.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — Protecting Data at Rest

option_description: Attestation that volume/rate anomalies (rows-read-per-minute, full-table-scan bursts, large result-set transfers, mass S3 GetObject) emit alerts consistent with T1213 bulk-harvest detection.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Broken authorization at the crossing - over-privileged grants enabling bulk harvesting" (T1213) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when bulk_read_volume_anomaly_alerted is false. Without volume monitoring, an authorised identity scraping the entire dataset looks identical to normal traffic.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SIEM / monitoring rules for the data tier. Confirm explicit detections exist for: rows-read-per-minute per principal, full-table-scan bursts, large result-set transfers, S3 GetObject volume spikes per identity.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SIEM contains named correlation rules (e.g., 'bulk-read-T1213', 's3-mass-get') with explicit thresholds, owners, and on-call routing.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1213 Data from Information Repositories

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS data tiers, confirm CloudWatch metric filters or GuardDuty findings cover S3 mass-download and RDS Performance Insights anomalies; confirm alarms route to an on-call destination.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --query 'MetricAlarms[?contains(AlarmName,`bulk`) || contains(AlarmName,`exfil`)]' ; aws guardduty list-findings --finding-criteria '{"Criterion":{"type":{"Eq":["Exfiltration:S3/AnomalousBehavior"]}}}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Named alarms exist with InsufficientDataActions/OKActions/AlarmActions routing to SNS pager; GuardDuty has S3 protection enabled.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1213 Data from Information Repositories

how_to_obtain.instruction: Ask the SOC operator to walk through the last bulk-read alert: time-to-page, principal, response action. Tabletop a synthetic full-table scan and confirm it triggers a page within the documented SLO.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SOC produces an incident ticket from a real bulk-read alert OR a tabletop run that fired within the SLO; clear ownership recorded.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge

option_description: Attestation that DBA / break-glass access transits a recorded PAM / jump host (Teleport, BeyondTrust, AWS Session Manager) with MFA, time-boxed approval, and session recording. Direct DBA credentials are not held on workstations.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Boundary bypass via trusted DBA / management-path channel" (T1199, T1599) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when privileged_access_via_pam_with_session_recording is false. A phished DBA workstation walks straight into the data tier on a path that bypasses every app-tier control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Pull a sample of the last 10 DBA interventions from the ticketing system. Confirm each launched via the PAM portal with MFA, has a recorded session artefact, and originated from the PAM jump host's IP in the data-tier auth log — not a workstation.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 100% of DBA activity transits PAM with a recording artefact and MFA assertion; no successful data-tier login from a non-PAM source for any DBA role.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 12 Network Infrastructure Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Grep the data-tier auth log for any DBA-role login whose source IP is not the PAM jump host's CIDR. Any hit is a finding.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E 'usename=(dba|admin|postgres|root)' /var/log/postgresql/postgresql-*.log | awk '{print $N}' # filter source IP not in PAM CIDR
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Zero hits — every DBA-role login arrives from the PAM jump host CIDR range.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1078 Valid Accounts

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the PAM platform's role configuration for the DBA path: confirm MFA-required, time-boxed approval workflow, mandatory session recording, and that the approval requires a second human.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: DBA role on PAM platform has MFA enforced, recording=on, approval workflow with two-person rule, max session TTL <= 8h.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1021 Remote Services

option_description: Attestation that every management-plane path (mgmt VLAN, DBaaS support tunnel, monitoring agent, replication link, backup agent) enforces the same authn/authz/inspection as the primary app-tier crossing.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Boundary bypass via trusted DBA / management-path channel" (T1199, T1599) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when mgmt_paths_subject_to_same_pep_controls is false. A replication or monitoring channel that bridges the boundary without per-request authn becomes the attacker's preferred path.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List every non-application path that reaches the data tier: monitoring agents (Datadog, Prometheus exporters), backup agents, replication links (cross-region, cross-account), DBaaS vendor support tunnels, management VLANs. For each, document the authn/authz, encryption, and audit posture.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Every management path documented with explicit authn (per-agent identity, scoped IAM role) and audit destination; no path documented as 'trusted by network position'.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1599 Network Boundary Bridging

how_to_obtain.instruction: From a compromised-monitoring-agent perspective (simulate the agent's identity/network position), attempt to read or write outside the agent's narrow scope. Confirm the data tier refuses.
how_to_obtain.command: psql -h <data-host> -U datadog -c 'SELECT * FROM customer;' # should fail with insufficient privilege
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Agent identity is scoped — read attempts outside its narrow grant (e.g., pg_stat_*) are rejected; cannot read business tables.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-125B Secure Virtual Network Configuration for VM Protection

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect replication-link configuration (e.g., AWS RDS read-replica IAM, MongoDB replica-set keyFile, MinIO site replication) and confirm the replication principal is scoped to replication verbs and audit-logged identically to app traffic.
how_to_obtain.command: aws rds describe-db-instances --query 'DBInstances[*].ReadReplicaSourceDBInstanceIdentifier' ; mongod --config /etc/mongod.conf
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Replication principal is a dedicated, narrowly-scoped identity; replication channel TLS-encrypted; replication events appear in the same audit stream as app traffic.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture

option_description: Attestation that data-tier ingress rules scope source to a per-app workload identity (per-service security-group, SPIFFE SVID, per-app IAM DB role) — no flat 'app-tier -> all-databases' allow rule.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Lateral movement from a compromised peer workload" (T1021) — its sole OR-condition, firing when data_tier_ingress_scoped_per_workload_identity is false. A flat allow rule lets RCE in one app pivot east-west into a peer's database.

how_to_obtain.instruction: From inside workload A's pod/instance, attempt a TCP connect to workload B's data-store endpoint. Repeat across the service matrix (A->B, A->C, B->C, ...).
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl exec -it <pod-A> -- nc -zv <db-B-endpoint> 5432
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Cross-service connections are refused / filtered; only A->A-store and B->B-store paths open the TCP socket.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1021 Remote Services

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy / cloud security-group rules expressed in IaC. Confirm each data-store SG accepts only from the matching app's SG/service-account, not from a shared 'app-tier' SG.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get networkpolicy -A -o yaml ; aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids <db-sg> --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions[*].UserIdGroupPairs'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each data-store SG ingress lists only the matching app's SG ID (e.g., db-orders accepts from sg-app-orders only); no shared sg-app-tier appears.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-125B Secure Virtual Network Configuration for VM Protection

how_to_obtain.instruction: Walk the IaC repository (Terraform/Pulumi/CloudFormation) for the data-tier networking module. Confirm the source-of-truth defines per-service ingress, not just runtime-observed behaviour.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'security_group' <iac-repo>/data-tier/
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IaC declares per-service ingress with explicit source SG/role identifiers; no module-level for_each loop that produces a flat allow.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Network Segmentation Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attestation that app-to-data-store traffic crossing into the data tier is TLS-encrypted with a modern profile (TLS 1.2+, preferably 1.3); cleartext listeners are disabled.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Cleartext intra-VPC capture" (T1040) — its sole OR-condition, firing when data_tier_transit_encrypted is false. An attacker on any host with a path to the data-tier subnet sniffs credentials and queries from a private network that was assumed safe.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For each data engine, query the TLS configuration and confirm TLS is required (cleartext listeners disabled). PostgreSQL: SHOW ssl + pg_hba.conf hostssl. MySQL: require_secure_transport=ON. MongoDB: net.tls.mode=requireTLS. Redis: tls-port set + port=0. MinIO: --certs-dir populated.
how_to_obtain.command: psql -c 'SHOW ssl;' ; mysql -e "SHOW VARIABLES LIKE 'require_secure_transport';" ; redis-cli CONFIG GET tls-port ; redis-cli CONFIG GET port
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ssl=on / require_secure_transport=ON / requireTLS / tls-port set and port=0. No engine has an open cleartext listener.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Cryptographic Storage Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run an OpenSSL handshake against each data-tier endpoint and capture the negotiated protocol and cipher.
how_to_obtain.command: openssl s_client -connect <data-host>:5432 -starttls postgres ; openssl s_client -connect <data-host>:6380
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Handshake negotiates TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with a modern cipher (e.g., TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384). No SSLv3/TLS 1.0/1.1; no NULL or EXPORT ciphers.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-207 Zero Trust Architecture

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS RDS, confirm Force-SSL parameter group setting (rds.force_ssl=1 for Postgres, require_secure_transport=ON for MySQL) is attached and applied.
how_to_obtain.command: aws rds describe-db-parameters --db-parameter-group-name <pg> --query 'Parameters[?ParameterName==`rds.force_ssl`]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: rds.force_ssl=1 (or require_secure_transport=ON) is present, ApplyStatus=in-sync, attached to every in-scope instance.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — Protecting Data at Rest

option_description: Attestation that backups/snapshots are only written/copied/shared to pre-approved destinations within the boundary's trust scope — no public bucket, no untrusted cross-account share, no unrestricted region copy.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Backup / snapshot exfiltration outside the boundary" (T1552) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when backup_destinations_in_approved_region_and_account is false. A snapshot shared cross-account is silent data egress invisible to runtime controls.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate every snapshot and check for cross-account share permissions. Any non-self CreateVolumePermission or non-null AttributeValues principal is a finding.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --query 'Snapshots[?CreateVolumePermissions!=null]' ; aws rds describe-db-snapshots --query 'DBSnapshots[?AttributeValues!=null]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty array — no snapshot is shared with a non-trusted AWS account; no 'all' (public) principal anywhere.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the backup bucket's policy and ACL. Confirm no Principal:* and no public ACL grant; confirm bucket is in an approved region.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <backup-bucket> ; aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket <backup-bucket> ; aws s3api get-bucket-location --bucket <backup-bucket>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bucket policy contains no Principal:* statement; ACL lists only the bucket owner; LocationConstraint matches the approved-region allowlist.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — Protecting Data at Rest

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the AWS Backup vault access policy and confirm restore/copy/delete actions are scoped to the approved restore role and the destination region list is bounded.
how_to_obtain.command: aws backup get-backup-vault-access-policy --backup-vault-name <vault> ; aws backup list-backup-vaults
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Vault policy restricts backup:CopyIntoBackupVault and backup:StartRestoreJob to a dedicated restore-role ARN; destination regions enumerated, not wildcard.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

how_to_obtain.instruction: For MinIO/S3-compatible object stores, confirm no anonymous read on the backup bucket.
how_to_obtain.command: mc anonymous get ALIAS/backup-bucket
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output reads 'private' (or 'none') — no anonymous policy is attached to the backup bucket.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

option_description: Attestation that the backup/snapshot channel emits its own audit trail (snapshot share events, backup-vault policy changes, cross-region copies) to a tamper-resistant store outside data-tier admin scope.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Backup / snapshot exfiltration outside the boundary" (T1552) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when backup_egress_audited_separately is false. Without backup-channel audit, exfiltration via snapshot share is invisible to the primary data-tier monitoring.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm CloudTrail (or equivalent) is enabled, multi-region, and logging ModifySnapshotAttribute, ModifyDBSnapshotAttribute, CopySnapshot, and PutBackupVaultAccessPolicy events to a centralised log account.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail describe-trails --query 'trailList[*].[Name,IsMultiRegionTrail,S3BucketName]' ; aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name <trail>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Trail is multi-region with IsLogging=true; event selectors capture management events including snapshot-attribute and backup-vault changes; destination S3 bucket lives in a centralised log account.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the centralised-log account S3 bucket policy denies write/delete from the data-tier account, and that object-lock or MFA-delete is enabled.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <log-bucket> ; aws s3api get-object-lock-configuration --bucket <log-bucket>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bucket policy denies s3:DeleteObject and s3:PutObject from the data-tier account; ObjectLockEnabled=Enabled with COMPLIANCE or GOVERNANCE retention.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

how_to_obtain.instruction: Walk the SIEM rule set for backup-channel events. Confirm explicit detections for: snapshot shared cross-account, backup-vault policy change, cross-region copy, deletion of backup recovery point.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SIEM has named correlation rules for each backup-channel event class; ownership and on-call route documented.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management

option_description: Attestation that principals authorised for KMS key-admin actions (ScheduleKeyDeletion, DisableKey, PutKeyPolicy, key export) are disjoint from principals operating the data store.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "KMS / key-administrator compromise (no separation of duties)" (T1552, T1485, T1078) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when kms_admin_separated_from_db_admin is false. A single identity that operates the DB and administers its KEK turns encryption-at-rest into decryption-at-will or a destructive ransom event.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Read the KMS key policy for every CMK wrapping data-tier storage. Enumerate the principals authorised for destructive actions (kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion, kms:DisableKey, kms:PutKeyPolicy, kms:Encrypt for re-wrap) and confirm they are disjoint from the DBA / data-tier operator role.
how_to_obtain.command: aws kms get-key-policy --key-id <CMK> --policy-name default
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Statements granting key-admin actions list a separate key-admin role/group; statements granting kms:Decrypt to the data-tier role do NOT also grant kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion / DisableKey / PutKeyPolicy.
how_to_obtain.source: AWS Well-Architected Security Pillar — Protecting Data at Rest

how_to_obtain.instruction: For each DBA / data-tier IAM role, evaluate effective KMS permissions across all attached and inline policies. Confirm no allow on destructive KMS actions.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/<dba-role> --action-names kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion kms:DisableKey kms:PutKeyPolicy
how_to_obtain.expected_output: EvalDecision=implicitDeny (or explicitDeny) for every destructive KMS action against the data-tier CMK; only kms:Decrypt / kms:GenerateDataKey are allowed.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Walk the org chart against IAM group membership. Confirm key-admins (security/cryptography team) and data-admins (platform/DBA team) are distinct humans, not just distinct roles assumed by the same person.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key-admin group and data-admin group have disjoint membership; documented separation-of-duties policy is signed off.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attestation that the wrapping KMS/HSM key has automated rotation enabled per documented cryptoperiod AND multi-party approval / pause window for destructive lifecycle actions (scheduled deletion, disable, export).
security_impact: Triggers exposure "KMS / key-administrator compromise (no separation of duties)" (T1552, T1485, T1078) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when kms_key_protection_policy_enforced is false. Without rotation + pause-window, a compromised key-admin schedules deletion and renders all data wrapped by the key permanently unrecoverable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query KMS key rotation status and confirm automatic rotation is enabled on every CMK wrapping data-tier storage.
how_to_obtain.command: aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <CMK>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: KeyRotationEnabled=true for every in-scope CMK; rotation cadence (annual default) documented.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the key's pending-window for ScheduleKeyDeletion is set to the maximum (30 days) so a compromised key-admin's deletion call can be reversed within the multi-party-approval window. Also confirm a CloudWatch alarm/EventBridge rule fires on kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion to a separate on-call.
how_to_obtain.command: aws kms describe-key --key-id <CMK> --query 'KeyMetadata.[PendingWindowInDays,DeletionDate]' ; aws events list-rules --query 'Rules[?contains(Name,`kms-delete`)]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: PendingWindowInDays=30 (or maximum allowed); EventBridge rule exists routing kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion / kms:DisableKey / kms:PutKeyPolicy events to an out-of-band pager.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-209 Security Guidelines for Storage Infrastructure

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the key-policy and any SCP for a require-MFA condition (aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent) on destructive actions, and confirm the runbook documents multi-party approval for key disable/delete/export.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key policy / SCP carries Condition:{Bool:{aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent:true}} on destructive actions; runbook requires two named approvers; cryptoperiod and rotation interval explicitly stated.
how_to_obtain.source: OWASP Key Management Cheat Sheet

option_description: Attestation that every data-tier crossing (successful connection, failed auth, DDL, DML at sensitivity threshold) is logged and ships to a tamper-resistant store outside DBA administrative scope.
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Unmonitored crossings - audit gap at the boundary" (T1562, T1070) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when data_tier_crossings_audit_logged_to_tamper_resistant_store is false. Logs kept inside DBA scope can be wiped by an attacker who reaches that scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For each data engine, confirm connection + DDL/DML logging is enabled. PostgreSQL: log_connections / log_disconnections / log_statement / pgaudit config. MySQL: general_log + audit_log plugin. MongoDB: auditLog in db.getCmdLineOpts(). AWS RDS: EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports.
how_to_obtain.command: psql -c "SHOW log_connections;" -c "SHOW log_disconnections;" -c "SHOW log_statement;" ; mongosh --eval 'db.getCmdLineOpts().parsed.auditLog' ; aws rds describe-db-instances --query 'DBInstances[*].EnabledCloudwatchLogsExports'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: log_connections=on, log_disconnections=on, log_statement=ddl (at minimum); pgaudit.log includes 'role,ddl,write'; RDS exports ['postgresql','upgrade'] or equivalent to CloudWatch.
how_to_obtain.source: PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 10 — Log and Monitor All Access

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the log destination is a centralised log account / SIEM outside the DBA's IAM scope. Confirm the destination bucket has object-lock or equivalent write-once protection.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-object-lock-configuration --bucket <log-bucket> ; aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <log-bucket>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Destination bucket lives in a log-archive account; ObjectLockEnabled=Enabled; bucket policy denies Put/Delete from the data-tier account.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AU-9 Protection of Audit Information

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify with the DBA team that they cannot delete or alter shipped logs — they can read for diagnostics but cannot purge. Attempt a delete from a DBA principal as a falsification test.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api delete-object --bucket <log-bucket> --key <test-key> # invoked under DBA principal
how_to_obtain.expected_output: AccessDenied — the DBA principal cannot delete from the log archive. Confirms tamper-resistance.
how_to_obtain.source: NIST SP 800-92 Guide to Computer Security Log Management

option_description: Attestation that failed authentication attempts and privileged / admin events (role/grant changes, DDL, bulk-read anomalies) generate alerts on a defined path (SIEM, pager).
security_impact: Triggers exposure "Unmonitored crossings - audit gap at the boundary" (T1562, T1070) — one of its OR-conditions, firing when failed_auth_and_admin_events_alerted is false. Logging without alerting means brute-force, privilege escalation, and DDL go unnoticed in real time.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the SIEM detection rule set for the data tier. Confirm named rules for: failed-auth-burst-per-principal, GRANT/REVOKE/CREATE USER, DDL on production schemas, role membership change.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SIEM produces a list of named correlation rules covering each event class above, with thresholds and on-call routing configured.
how_to_obtain.source: CIS Controls v8 Control 8 Audit Log Management

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS-managed databases, confirm CloudWatch metric filters / alarms exist for FailedSQLServerAuthentications (or equivalent log-derived metric) and for IAM auth failures, routing to an SNS pager.
how_to_obtain.command: aws logs describe-metric-filters --log-group-name /aws/rds/instance/<id>/postgresql ; aws cloudwatch describe-alarms --query 'MetricAlarms[?contains(AlarmName,`auth`) || contains(AlarmName,`failed`)]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Metric filters extract 'authentication failed' patterns; alarms fire on threshold breach with AlarmActions pointing at the on-call SNS topic.
how_to_obtain.source: MITRE ATT&CK T1078 Valid Accounts

how_to_obtain.instruction: Tabletop: generate 20 failed-auth attempts against the data tier from a test workload. Confirm a page reaches the on-call within the documented SLO.
how_to_obtain.command: for i in {1..20}; do PGPASSWORD=wrong psql -h <data-host> -U app_orders -c 'SELECT 1'; done
how_to_obtain.expected_output: On-call receives a page within the documented detection SLO (typically <=5 min); the alert names the principal and source IP.
how_to_obtain.source: general-knowledge
